espn-604000.headline: Winless Italy are one result from passing Wales
beats: Italy have no points from four Nations Championship games, and they conceded 66, 57 and 47 in their last three. Beat Argentina in Genova and they rise to 9th in the world, above Fiji and above Wales, who beat them 31–17 in March.

Argentina arrive as favourites with one win in 2026 and a 42–12 loss in Dublin. Felipe Contepomi, heavily criticised by the Argentine press, says winning matters but must come through a path of stability. That is a hard sell after a run like this.
Pablo Matera captains in place of the injured Montoya and has picked a bench of six forwards and two backs. He rates Italy's set piece, then explains the bench: "È un pack pesante."
Italy host Fiji a week later, the only other side without a point. A win here would put Italy above Fiji in the world rankings before that game starts.

espn-604001.headline: New Zealand rest eight, and the streak dates from 1953
beats: Wales last beat New Zealand in 1953, and New Zealand have won the 34 meetings since. Dave Rennie has still changed eight of his starting XV for Cardiff, with six more among the replacements.

A year ago on this ground it was 24–21 to New Zealand in the 48th minute and 26–52 at the end. New Zealand have scored seven tries in each of their last three games, Scotland included. Wales beat Japan 28–21 last weekend in a game still in the balance near the finish.
Win and Wales go up to ninth, above Fiji. Rennie says New Zealand have talked about targeting Jac Morgan, the Lions flanker, which is a compliment of sorts.
Frank Bunce, once of New Zealand, admits "I couldn't name any of their players to be honest". Rennie, at least, can name one.

espn-604002.headline: Eddie Jones knows what England don't like
beats: Jones coached England from 2015 to 2022, longer than anyone else. He now brings a youthful Japan side to the Allianz Stadium promising to "play the house down", and has said his old side do not like "unorthodox" rugby.

Steve Borthwick has made 10 personnel changes after the 45–22 win over Australia, so his inexperienced side faces his predecessor's. England have never lost to Japan, and they scored a half-century of points in each of the two most recent meetings.

Japan lost by seven to Wales in Cardiff last week and lost to Fiji before that. Their way in is speed, which Maro Itoje says they are very consistent at getting into the game. A Japan win by 16 or more would drop England to sixth, below Scotland.
Jones says England have one eye on New Zealand a week later. Their scrum coach, Tom Harrison, says they do not. Only one of them gets to be right.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland get their South Africans a week early
beats: Jake White took over Fiji last month and brought Gert Smal with him. Smal was Ireland's forwards coach in the 2009 Grand Slam, so two South Africans sit in the visiting box before Ireland host South Africa on 21 November.
Andy Farrell has made seven changes, and the side is not a lesser one. Tadhg Beirne captains, Nick Timoney starts at 8 with Sean Jansen absent, and Jamison Gibson-Park is back at scrum-half.

Ireland ran in six tries against Argentina, 42–12, three of them by Hugo Keenan. Fiji conceded 54 to an injury-hit France in Lyon and have no points from four games. They did beat Japan away in October, which is more than Ireland's last opponents managed in Dublin.
A Fiji win would drop Ireland to fifth in the world, below France and England, with the Springboks next in line.

espn-604004.headline: Scotland's captain learned the game in a Melbourne backyard
beats: Sione Tuipulotu's sparring partner in that backyard was Isaac Kailea, who is on Australia's bench at Murrayfield. Tuipulotu was sin-binned in last week's 43–21 loss to New Zealand, when Scotland did not score after half-time.

Australia know that scoreline. They lost 21–43 to New Zealand in October, a week after conceding 50 to them, then let in 45 against England. Scotland have lost by 22 to Ireland and to New Zealand this year, and nobody has called that a coincidence.

Les Kiss recalls Carter Gordon, out since fracturing a leg in the 28–28 draw in Mendoza in September, and Rob Valetini. Kiss expects "Speed chess", and does not pretend to know what Scotland's fly-half will do: "When you've got Finn Russell, I don't think that's predictable at all."
Win, and Australia take Scotland's sixth place in the world rankings. Tuipulotu would rather Kailea did not get the last word in this one too.

espn-604005.headline: New Zealand's road back to No. 1 runs through London
beats: New Zealand were ranked first until 31 August, then lost twice in September to South Africa, 24–29 and 28–43. A win here by 16 or more puts them back above South Africa.
England are the side most likely to stop that. They beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025, a margin New Zealand would now need in reverse, plus two.

New Zealand have scored seven tries in each of their last three games, 50 in one of them and 43 in the other two. England scored seven against Australia, 45–22. In July they conceded 45 to South Africa.
Eddie Jones said England might already be distracted by New Zealand. He said it before his Japan side played them, which is one way of admitting where the week's attention was going.

espn-604006.headline: Japan bring Eddie Jones's curveballs to Murrayfield
beats: Japan go to Twickenham first, where Eddie Jones has promised his young side will "play the house down". England have put 50 on them in each of the last two meetings. Murrayfield is the next stop.

Scotland can sympathise. They have lost 21–43 twice this year, away to Ireland in March and at home to New Zealand on 7 November. Japan lost the same day in Wales, 21–28, close enough for a bonus point.
Scotland host Australia first, with Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn back in the side. Lose to Japan by 16 or more and Scotland drop to eighth, below Australia and Argentina.
Japan have nothing scheduled after this, so whatever Jones has left in the bag gets used here.

espn-604007.headline: Andrew Porter has had a year to think about that scrum
beats: South Africa won 24–13 in Dublin last November by taking Ireland's scrum apart: six penalties from 16 scrums, a penalty try, and four Irish players yellow-carded, Porter among them. Calf trouble has kept him out of an Ireland shirt ever since.
Ireland come in off a 42–12 win over Argentina, three of their six tries from Hugo Keenan. South Africa come from Paris, beaten 21–19 by France six days after putting 66 on Italy.
Lose again and South Africa slip below New Zealand to second in the world. Rassie Erasmus said after France that he would think about it all night.
James Tracy called Ireland's scrum that night ‘obliterated’. Porter's stated plan this time is to swing at it.

espn-604008.headline: Nought points each. At most one stays there
beats: Neither side has won in the championship: eight games between them, none won, and a combined points difference of minus 286. Italy lost 66–7 to South Africa at home on 7 November. Fiji shipped 54 to France the same day.
Fiji at least remember winning: 34–28 against Japan in October, with four tries. Italy have scored more than one try in only two of their last four.
Win, and Italy go from the bottom of the championship to 9th in the world, above both Fiji and Wales.
Italy then have Scotland away in February. Fiji's next Test after this is Spain in a World Cup pool in October 2027, which is a long time to sit on a loss.

espn-604009.headline: The hard part was the Springboks. Supposedly.
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19 on 13 November, Louis Bielle-Biarrey scoring a try and making the last tackle that kept it. Fabien Galthié said afterwards he had heard his side would be rolled over.
Argentina arrive with one win in 2026, against Wales, and were beaten 42–12 in Ireland last time out. Their squad is drawn mostly from the Top 14, so the Stade de France will hold few strangers.
France come in depleted. Julien Marchand withdrew minutes before the Springbok game with a thigh problem. Win this and the route to the Nations Championship final stays in their own hands.
Lose, and France drop below England to fifth in the world, which is not what beating the champions was for.

espn-604010.headline: Wales scraped past Japan; Australia shipped 45 at Twickenham
beats: Australia have conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand, then 45 to England on 8 November. Before Cardiff, Les Kiss has Murrayfield, where Joseph Suaalii moves back to outside centre.

Wales are hardly a fortress. The BBC described them as "spluttering" to a 28-21 win over Japan, with morale low after constant off-field turmoil. New Zealand visit first, and the bookmakers have Wales at 20-1.
Wales did score four tries against Japan, and Australia have been leaking far more than that. Win, and Wales climb to ninth while Australia drop to eighth, below Argentina.
Wales go to France in February. Australia's next Test is Hong Kong at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to replay a bad afternoon.
